r0.why: Carbon in diamond cubic structure [1]; tasteless, odorless, strong, brittle, poor conductor, colorless, insoluble [2].

r1.why: Allotropes [24], diamond and graphite most common [25], four neighbours in tetrahedra [27], rigid, most atoms per volume so hardest and least compressible [28].

r2.why: Heading 'The same element, much softer' states graphite is the same element (carbon) as diamond; cited [26],[30],[31] never say graphite is carbon (that is in uncited [3]/[25]).

r3.why: Ages [8], mantle depths [9], carbon fluids replacing minerals [10], eruptions to kimberlites and lamproites [11].

r4.why: Graphite stable at room conditions [3]; metastable diamond, energy barrier, negligible rate over millions to billions of years [42]; rapid above 4500 K [43].

r5.why: Rigid lattice admits few impurities, boron and nitrogen exceptions [5]; one per million and the colour causes [6].

r6.why: Lavoisier 1772 lens and carbon dioxide [20], Tennant 1797 [21], same gas from diamond and graphite showing equivalence [22].

r7.why: Highest hardness and thermal conductivity used in cutting and polishing tools [4], synthetic growth routes [12], distinguishing methods [13].
